title: Slip and Fall in the Lobby

opening.text: LP, front desk. A lady's fallen just inside the street doors. It's wet, it's pouring outside. She's sitting up but she's holding her wrist. Can you come?

briefing: 22:15. Heavy rain. A guest has slipped on the marble inside the street doors. You are the Assistant LP Manager and claims files are yours.

Veldane claims practice: the person first. Then make the area safe, record the scene before it is cleaned, take statements from witnesses and staff, keep the footage, and report to the insurer. Be kind and helpful; do not admit liability or promise payment. Your authority is 10,000.
learningObjectives: The person first: care, first aid, the offer of an ambulance
Record the scene before it changes: photographs, measurements, footage, statements
Empathy without admitting liability; the insurer's first notice

actions.label: See to the guest
actions.finding: She came in from a taxi at 22:12, stepped off the mat and her feet went from under her. She landed on her right hand: the wrist is swelling and painful to move; no head strike, no other pain. She is a guest in 1022, at the conference. Shaken, embarrassed, then angry.

lines.speaker: guest_ashcombe
lines.text: I stepped off the mat and the floor just went. It's like ice. My wrist, I can't bend it.

actions.label: First aid and the offer of an ambulance
actions.finding: A cold pack and a sling from the first aid kit, a chair, a glass of water. You offer an ambulance; she declines and asks for a taxi to the Harbour General's urgent care. The desk books one on the hotel's account. You note her refusal and the time.

actions.label: Cone off the wet floor
actions.finding: Two wet floor cones and a barrier around the wet patch; arrivals routed along the mat. The patch is not touched until it is recorded.

actions.label: Photograph and measure the scene
finding: Wide and close photographs with a scale: a wet patch 1.8 m by 1.1 m on polished marble, 40 cm beyond the edge of the entrance mat. The mat has been pushed 60 cm to the side and its corner is folded.
No wet floor sign was out. Her shoes: low heels with smooth soles, wet. Lighting good. Time on every photograph.

actions.label: Have the floor dried and the mat put back
actions.finding: The night cleaner dries the marble and lays the mat back across the full width of the doors. The cones stay until the floor is dry.

actions.label: Take Tariq's statement
actions.finding: He saw her come in, step to the left of the mat and fall at about 22:13. He noticed the mat had been moved earlier "for a luggage trolley" but did not put it back. No sign was out. He signs and dates it.

actions.label: Ask Owen about the mat
actions.finding: At about 21:50 he pushed the mat aside to get a loaded luggage cart in from a coach, "meant to put it straight back", then got called away. He signs a statement.

lines.speaker: bell_captain
lines.text: The cart catches on the mat. I pushed it over for one trip. I should have put it back. That's on me.

actions.label: Check the public areas cleaning and rain log
actions.finding: The lobby was last checked at 21:30. The rain procedure (extra mats, signs at the doors, checks every 20 minutes when it rains) was not started tonight: the log shows no rain entry at all.

actions.label: Review and preserve the street door camera
actions.finding: 21:51 the bell captain drags the mat aside for a luggage cart. Between 21:55 and 22:12 eleven people walk in from the rain over the bare marble; two slip and recover. 22:12:48 Ms Ashcombe steps off the taxi, walks in, falls at 22:13:02. Exported with a hash and logged.
rows: Mat pushed aside for a luggage cart
Eleven arrivals over the wet marble; two slip and recover

actions.label: Send the insurer the first notice of loss
actions.finding: Odile Marchetti opens a general liability file: date, time, place, injury as reported, ambulance declined, photographs, two statements, footage preserved. She asks that nobody discusses fault or payment with the guest and that all contact goes through the duty manager and her.

lines.speaker: adjuster
lines.text: Photographs before cleaning and the footage already preserved. That's a file I can work with. Please, nothing about fault to the guest.

actions.label: Promise Ms Ashcombe the hotel will cover everything
actions.finding: She thanks you and writes down your name. The insurer will read it in her lawyer's letter.

schedules.description: Mrs Ashcombe's solicitor quotes your promise at the scene that the hotel would cover everything. Tarrowby reserves its position on the claim and the hotel carries more of the cost.

questions.prompt: "Your floor's a death trap. Who's going to pay for this?" What do you say?

options.label: "I'm sorry you've been hurt. Let's get your wrist looked at first. I'm recording exactly what happened, and the duty manager will contact you tomorrow about what happens next."
options.feedback: Sorry for her pain is kindness, not an admission. You told her the truth about what happens next and promised nothing you don't control.

reply.speaker: guest_ashcombe
reply.text: Fine. Thank you. I just want my wrist seen to.

options.label: "The hotel will take care of everything, I promise."
options.feedback: Kind, but an admission and a promise you have no authority to make.

options.label: "It's raining. People need to watch where they step."
options.feedback: Blaming her is unkind, untrue on the evidence, and the first thing her lawyer will quote.

reply.speaker: guest_ashcombe
reply.text: Are you serious? Get me your manager.

questions.prompt: She declines an ambulance. What do you do?

options.label: Respect it, advise her to be seen tonight, arrange the taxi, and record the offer, the refusal and the time.
options.feedback: Her choice, your advice and a record of both.

options.label: Call one anyway.
options.feedback: She is alert and decides for herself. Calling against her wishes takes a crew from someone who needs it.

options.label: Leave it; she said she's fine.
options.feedback: No advice and no record. If her wrist is broken, the file shows nothing offered.

questions.prompt: What do you spend so it doesn't happen again?

options.label: Full-width entrance mats fixed into the floor, a second mat for rain, and the rain procedure on the duty checklist: about 6,800.
options.feedback: Fixes the cause (mats that move, a procedure nobody started) within your authority.

options.label: Replace the lobby marble with a textured stone: about 120,000.
options.feedback: A capital project far above your authority, for a problem mats and a procedure solve.

options.label: A permanent "Caution: wet floor" sign by the doors.
options.feedback: Signs that are always out stop being read, and it doesn't stop the mat being moved.

options.label: 22:13 a guest slipped on wet marble 40 cm beyond the entrance mat, which had been moved aside at 21:51; right wrist injury reported; ambulance declined; scene photographed before cleaning; footage preserved.
options.feedback: Facts, times and what was recorded, without blame or a conclusion on fault.

options.label: Guest fell because the bell captain moved the mat.
options.feedback: A conclusion on fault. Record the facts; cause and liability are for the insurer.

options.label: Guest in unsuitable shoes slipped in the rain.
options.feedback: Selective and blaming. Her shoes are in the photographs; let the facts speak.

questions.prompt: Claims file, which of these belong in it?

options.label: Photographs LP-PH-1402 with scale: wet patch 1.8 x 1.1 m, mat displaced 60 cm, corner folded, no sign out.
L-01: mat moved 21:51; eleven arrivals over wet marble, two slips; fall at 22:13:02. Exported and hashed.
Signed statements: Tariq Bello (witness), Owen Tremlett (moved the mat).
Public areas log: last check 21:30, rain procedure not started.
LP apologised on behalf of the hotel for its negligence.
options.feedback: That never happened and must never be written: it is an admission of liability.

checks.label: The person first
checks.pass: You saw to her before you photographed anything.
checks.fail: You recorded the scene while she sat there hurt.

checks.label: Make it safe
checks.pass: The patch was coned off before anyone else fell.
checks.fail: The wet floor stayed open to arrivals.

checks.label: Record before cleaning
checks.pass: The scene was photographed and measured before it was dried.
checks.fail: The floor was cleaned before it was recorded: the claim will turn on memory.

checks.label: Keep the footage
checks.pass: The door camera was reviewed and preserved tonight.
checks.fail: The footage was never kept and will overwrite.

checks.label: Statements
checks.pass: The staff member who moved the mat gave a signed statement.
checks.fail: Nobody asked why the mat was out of place.

checks.label: No admission
checks.pass: Kind, helpful, and no promise about payment or fault.
checks.fail: You promised payment you have no authority to promise.

checks.label: First notice
checks.pass: The insurer had the first notice with the evidence the same night.

checks.label: Why was it wet?
checks.pass: The log showed the rain procedure never started.
checks.fail: You never checked why the floor was wet and unsigned.

debrief.whatHappened: A bell captain moved the entrance mat for a luggage cart in the rain and nobody put it back or started the rain procedure. Twenty minutes later a guest stepped onto bare wet marble and broke her fall with her wrist. You cared for her, recorded the scene before it was cleaned, and gave the insurer a file it can defend or settle fairly.
bestPractice: See to the person first; offer first aid and an ambulance and record the answer.
Make the area safe without cleaning it, then photograph and measure with a scale.
Take signed statements from witnesses and the staff involved.
Review and preserve the footage; check the cleaning and inspection logs.
Empathy, yes; admission of fault or promises of payment, no.
Give the insurer first notice the same day, with the evidence.
Fix the cause: fixed mats and a rain procedure someone owns.
debrief.why: Slip and fall claims are the most common liability claims a hotel has. The ones that go badly are the ones with no photographs, no footage and a staff member's promise in the guest's notes.
commonMistakes: No statement from the staff member involved.

lesson: Person first, record before you clean, kind words without admissions.
